sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR  ORAL ORDER

The petitioners-accused Nos. 1 and 2 who have been charge-sheeted for offences punishable under Sections 465, 468, 471, 419, 420, and 201 of the IPC, have approached this Court challenging the order of the Trial Court, wherein their application filed under Section 239 of the Cr.PC seeking discharge was dismissed.

2. The prosecution alleges that accused No. 1 conveyed the subject land to accused No. 2, who then engaged the services of accused No. 3 to obtain a no-objection certificate from the competent authority, certifying that no proceedings were pending under Sections 79(A) and 79(B) of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.
It is alleged that the petitioners fraudulently obtained the said certificate by forging the seal and signature of the complainant, i.e., the Assistant Commissioner.

The petitioners filed an application for discharge, primarily on the ground that the complainant had communicated that they were not involved in the fabrication of documents, which was instead carried out by a third person.
Despite this, the police, while arraigning the third person as accused No. 3, also filed the charge sheet against accused Nos. 1 and 2.
The Trial Court rejected their application, prompting the petitioners to approach this Court.

sentences.text: 4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

5. The complainant, i.e., the Assistant Commissioner, issued a communication dated 18.06.2016 (document No. 8) to the Investigating Officer, stating that accused Nos. 1 and 2 were not involved in the fabrication of documents and that the fabrication was carried out by a third person.
The petitioners had merely engaged the services of accused No. 3 to obtain the no-objection certificate from the complainant.
Upon noticing this, the Assistant Commissioner issued a communication recommending that the investigation against accused Nos. 1 and 2 be dropped.

The said communication forms part of the charge sheet .However, instead of proceeding against the third person who was actually involved in the fabrication, the Investigating Officer continued the investigation against the petitioners despite the absence of substantive evidence to support the allegations against them.

6. In such circumstances, the continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners, in the absence of any material NC: 2025:KHC:10356 evidence to substantiate the allegations, would amount to an abuse of the process of law.
7. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

The impugned order dated 9.5.2024 passed on the application filed under Section 239 by the learned II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kolar is hereby set aside, and the application for discharge is allowed.
The petitioners are discharged of the aforesaid offences.
